<sub>[events.go](../../events.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.IssuerEvents"></a>

### limes.IssuerEvents

```go
type IssuerEvents struct {
	// OnIssued is called for every token minted: by Issue, Delegate,
	// Reissue and Biscuit, which IssuedEvent.Operation tells apart.
	OnIssued func(context.Context, IssuedEvent)
	// OnRefused is called for every request the issuer refused: one
	// malformed, too wide, naming what is not on record, or deriving from a
	// capability expired or revoked.
	OnRefused func(context.Context, IssuerErrorEvent)
	// OnFailed is called for every call that failed for the server's own
	// reasons: a store or a signer that failed, or a feature not configured.
	OnFailed func(context.Context, IssuerErrorEvent)
}
```

IssuerEvents are the callbacks an Issuer makes as it works (IssuerConfig.Events), for metrics or an audit sink beside its log. Each is optional. They run synchronously, on the caller's goroutine, after the outcome is logged and before the method returns: a callback must not block, and must not panic — the issuer does not recover one.

The callbacks are independent: each outcome calls one of them, and a nil one drops its events without a word. An audit sink that must see every call sets OnIssued, OnRefused and OnFailed all. ADR-0021 records the design.

<a id="limes.RevokedEvent"></a>

### limes.RevokedEvent

```go
type RevokedEvent struct {
	// Operation is the method called.
	Operation RevokerOperation
	// CapabilityID is the capability Revoke revoked, or whose Biscuit copy
	// RevokeBiscuit revoked; uuid.Nil() for RevokeMatching.
	CapabilityID uuid.UUID
	// TenantID is the tenant RevokeMatching was scoped to; uuid.Nil() for
	// one across every tenant, and for the other operations.
	TenantID uuid.UUID
	// Actor and Note are the request's, as stored for audit.
	Actor, Note string
	// AlreadyRevoked reports, for Revoke and RevokeBiscuit, that the
	// capability or the copy had an entry before the call, which wrote none.
	AlreadyRevoked bool
	// PriorDisposition is Revoke's RevokeResult.PriorDisposition.
	PriorDisposition RecordDisposition
	// Revoked, Tenants and More are RevokeMatching's RevokeMatchingResult:
	// the entries it wrote, the tenants it wrote them in — a copy, the
	// callback's own — and whether more may match.
	Revoked int64
	Tenants []uuid.UUID
	More    bool
	// Duration is the call's elapsed time, from its entry to the outcome,
	// on the monotonic clock.
	Duration time.Duration
}
```

RevokedEvent is one call a Revoker carried out.

### limes.RevokerEvents

```go
type RevokerEvents struct {
	// OnRevoked is called for every call the store carried out: by Revoke,
	// RevokeMatching and RevokeBiscuit, which RevokedEvent.Operation tells
	// apart — a repeat that wrote nothing among them.

	// OnRefused is called for every request the store refused: one
	// malformed, or naming what is not on record or not visible.
	OnRefused func(context.Context, RevokerErrorEvent)
	// OnFailed is called for every call that failed for the server's own
	// reasons: a store that failed, or a feature not configured.
	OnFailed func(context.Context, RevokerErrorEvent)
}
```

<a id="limes.VerifierEvents"></a>

### limes.VerifierEvents

```go
type VerifierEvents struct {
	// OnVerified is called for every token the verifier accepted: by
	// Verify, Authorize, Introspect and BiscuitCopy.
	OnVerified func(context.Context, VerifiedEvent)
	// OnRefused is called for every token the verifier refused, whatever
	// the reason: the reason is in the event.
	OnRefused func(context.Context, VerifierErrorEvent)
	// OnFailed is called for every check that failed for the server's own
	// reasons: the keys or the revocations out of reach, a replay cache that
	// failed, a feature not configured.
	OnFailed func(context.Context, VerifierErrorEvent)
}
```

VerifierEvents are the callbacks a Verifier makes as it checks tokens (VerifierConfig.Events), for metrics or an audit sink beside its log. Each is optional. They run synchronously, on the caller's goroutine — every request the verifier checks waits for them — after the outcome is logged and before the method returns: a callback must not block, and must not panic — the verifier does not recover one.

The callbacks are independent: each outcome calls one of them, and a nil one drops its events without a word. An audit sink that must see every check sets OnVerified, OnRefused and OnFailed all. ADR-0021 records the design.

<a id="otelmetric"></a><a id="package-otelmetric"></a>

## Package otelmetric

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/otelmetric"`

Package otelmetric wraps a meter.UsageStore in OpenTelemetry instruments: charge, settle, refund, reservation and request-count measurements, by outcome and unit, and a capability's spend after each charge. It is a module of its own so that limes itself never resolves an OpenTelemetry dependency; a consumer that wants the metrics adds this one.

The limes.outcome attribute is one of allowed; overrun, committed past a ceiling under meter.OverrunPolicyRecord; budget\_exceeded; tenant\_budget\_exceeded; request\_limit\_exceeded, a request limit or a Biscuit copy past its quota (meter.ErrCopyLimitExceeded), on a Bump, Charge, Settle or Reserve alike; and error. A refusal for a limit also carries limes.scope, which ceiling refused it: capability (its own or an ancestor's), lease, copy or tenant.

The instruments: limes.charge.amount and limes.refund.amount, by limes.unit\_code; limes.charge.decisions (charges and settles), limes.reservation.decisions and limes.request.bumps, by limes.outcome and limes.scope; and limes.charge.current\_spend, a histogram of a capability's spend after each charge, by limes.unit\_code. A limit refuses on whichever counter the call it refused counts on — a Bump on limes.request.bumps, a Charge or Settle on limes.charge.decisions, a Reserve on limes.reservation.decisions — so an alert on every limit reads all three, by limes.scope.

	usage, err := otelmetric.Instrument(store,
		otelmetric.WithMeterProvider(provider), // default: the global provider
		otelmetric.WithTenantAttribute(),       // opt-in: one series per tenant
	)

Instruments are created per store, and an error creating them is returned. A replayed charge or settle moved nothing and is not counted. limes.tenant\_id is off by default, as it multiplies every series by the number of tenants; with WithTenantAttribute every measurement, a refused charge or settle among them, carries the subject's tenant.

NewStoreEvents returns the callbacks a usage store reports to (pgstore.Config.Events): limes.tenant.wait, a histogram in seconds of how long each metered call waited for its tenant's row — the aggregate's, or its stripe's where the store stripes an unlimited tenant — by limes.operation, the store call:

	events, err := otelmetric.NewStoreEvents(otelmetric.WithMeterProvider(provider))
	store, err := pgstore.NewUsageStore(pgstore.Config{DB: pool, Events: events})

InstrumentRevocationCache reports a limes.RevocationCache's counts — hits, misses, upstream lookups, evictions, stale answers and entries, each by kind (capability or biscuit), its clears, whole and narrow, and the revocation signal: whether lineage and a signal vouch for it, the signal's connections, losses and notifications — as observable instruments, read only when the provider collects:

	reg, err := otelmetric.InstrumentRevocationCache(cache,
		otelmetric.WithMeterProvider(provider))
	defer reg.Unregister()

<a id="otelmetric.Instrument"></a>

### otelmetric.Instrument

```go
func Instrument(inner meter.UsageStore, opts ...Option) (meter.UsageStore, error)
```

Instrument wraps a meter.UsageStore in OpenTelemetry instruments. Its instruments are created on the global MeterProvider unless WithMeterProvider names another, and carry no tenant unless WithTenantAttribute asks for it.

The result implements every interface of package meter that inner does — the optional meter.CopyUsageReader, meter.TenantUsageEraser, meter.MatchingReleaser, meter.TenantReservationLister and meter.Leaser — and forwards meter.FeatureGate, so wrapping a store never hides what it can do, nor turns on what its configuration turned off. The decorator forwards a fixed list of optional interfaces (internal/optionalgen), and a test fails when the list misses one the store has.

<sub>[otelmetric/store.go](../../otelmetric/store.go)</sub>
<a id="otelmetric.InstrumentRevocationCache"></a>

### otelmetric.InstrumentRevocationCache

```go
func InstrumentRevocationCache(cache *limes.RevocationCache, opts ...Option) (metric.Registration, error)
```

InstrumentRevocationCache reports cache's counts (limes.RevocationCacheStats) as observable instruments, read each time the provider collects, so the cache's checks pay nothing for them. Unregister the registration it returns to stop. Of the options, only WithMeterProvider applies: the cache's counts have no tenant.

<sub>[otelmetric/cache.go](../../otelmetric/cache.go)</sub>
<a id="otelmetric.NewStoreEvents"></a>

### otelmetric.NewStoreEvents

```go
func NewStoreEvents(opts ...Option) (meter.StoreEvents, error)
```

NewStoreEvents returns the callbacks a usage store reports to as it works (pgstore.Config.Events), recorded as instruments: limes.tenant.wait, a histogram of how long each metered call waited for its tenant's row, in seconds, by limes.operation, and by limes.tenant\_id under WithTenantAttribute. The wait is for that row alone — the aggregate's, or the tenant's stripe where the store stripes an unlimited tenant — not for the tenant's advisory lock nor for the counters of the call's chain (docs/adr/0022-unlimited-tenant-aggregate.md, Decision 6).
